designed.text: Each claim on this site carries a status and the sources that give it that status. The unit a reader or an agent would pay for is not the page but the claim with its evidence chain: 'is this use of it sound', in the newsroom's phrase, not 'is this true'. Proposed price: 1p per claim read, 5p per claim with its captures opened, 20p per claim re-verified on request.

The newsroom's economics page argues a 60/25/10/5 split between the creator of the fact, the checker, the publisher and the rails. On this site the creators are the agencies, the researchers and the reporters whose pages are captured; the checker is the collector agent and the verifier; the publisher is this site. The split is argued, not implemented: nothing here pays anyone.

A reader who wants the bytes rather than this site's reading of them would be sold a read-only snapshot of the evidence vault for a fixed sum, opened in the browser with a read key. The captures are third-party pages and are not for republication, so this stays a proposal until the rights question has an answer.

An agent that briefs an executive every morning would pay per briefing regenerated, metered by the same component, with the balance kept in the agent's own vault rather than a browser. The meter already fires an event per charge; nothing listens to it here.

cost_model.note: A model of what this story cost to assemble, in units counted from the vault and the repository. The unit prices are assumptions, labelled as such; the counts are not.

units.why: one headless-browser capture with six files and their hashes
the same page captured again is a new unit, because the series is the record
an agent reading a page and writing what it says, who says it and what is odd
one claim, its status and its sources
one event, its time, its source and whether the time was stated or converted
the build is deterministic and costs nothing to run again

pricing.formula: price = max(floor, round(base[type] x freshness[tier])), then x the share of the page read (never under a tenth) x the reader's usefulness rating

types.why: A conclusion someone signed, written against a stated state of the evidence: the most judgement per word on the site.
The most compressed form of the work: one page for one reader's decision.

types.pages: the claims, the numbers, the agencies, affected systems, the code, the review, in context
types.why: Work a reader cannot do by reading one source: counting, comparing, converting times, reading the code.

types.pages: the front page, the flaws, the timeline, the leak, discovery, exploitation, impact, defence, the playbook, the questions
types.why: Pages assembled from the vault by agents; the reader pays for the assembly.

types.pages: every source and its page, the inventory, the parties, the graph
types.why: Reference pages: the value is in checking, and checking must never cost more at the moment it matters most.

types.pages: the method, the team, the billing model, the brief, corrections, the layers, the article index, admin
types.why: The site's account of itself. Metered at the floor, because the editor asked for no free pages, and never more, because a reader checking how the site works should not be charged for checking.

types.pages: your reading account, top up, topped up
types.why: The meter's own pages. Charging a reader to see their bill is not a price; the one exception to no free pages.

tiers.why: The first day: when the content is news and a reader is deciding something now.
The first week: still the current state of a developing story.
The base price: settled enough to rely on, recent enough to act on.
The record: worth reading, priced for the reader doing history, never free.

pricing.age_from: The date the page's content last changed: for a rebuilt page, the time of the latest capture its data comes from (so new evidence makes a page fresh again); for an article, the date it was written (so an article only ever ages).
rules: Every content page is metered. The only unmetered pages are the meter's own: your account, top up and topped up.
The price depends on two things only: what kind of content the page is, and how fresh it is. Not on who is reading, not on demand, not on the topic.
Fresh costs more and the price halves into the archive, never to zero. Evidence and the site's account of itself do not decay and stay at the floor.
A page costs its price times the share of it you read, never less than a tenth; once per page per session; rating it re-prices it from free to double.
Nothing is ever blocked. The balance can go below zero, and a reader can decline to pay and say why.
The age is worked out in your browser from the date on the page; the build has no clock, so the same release serves the same prices table to everyone.
The prices table is published here and generated from the same data file as the meter, so the page and the meter cannot disagree.
